$$
\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{3} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$"] [:db/add "fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/answer-fields $$" :question/worked-solution "Let's introduce the new variable $u= 1-x^4.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\dfrac{ \textrm{d}u}{ \textrm{d}x} = -4x^3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^3 \, \textrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{4} \textrm{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int {x^3\,{3^{1-x^4}} }\, \textrm{d}x 
&=\int {{3^{1-x^4}}\cdot x^3 }\, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt]
&=  \int {3^{u}} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \textrm{d}u\\[5pt]
                                                     &= -\dfrac{1}{4}\int {3^{u}}  \textrm{d}u\\[5pt]
                                                     &=  -\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{3^{u}}{\ln 3} + C\\[5pt]
